Welcome! If you're new to the game, fear not! We have a new player introduction video and game guide that will help you through the basics of Town of Salem 2. We suggest you try out the Classic game mode for your first few games.

You died! That's okay though. You gained some Ghost Points! You get those everytime you die. You can use them to play minigames or place guesses on the game! You can access the ghost games menu in the dock.

Special Abilities You can hover your mouse over, or tap, the icon to read about what the Special Ability does. If it has chains on it, it cannot be used. This can be because the Special Ability can only be used at certain phases of the game (such as night, or day). The glowing circles represent the number of uses an Ability has. If there is an infinity sign (∞) that means the Special Ability has unlimited uses.

Role Cards You can hover your mouse over, or tap, the different icons on your Role Card to discover how your role works. You can view your Attack and Defense, the role summary, attributes, and the abilities of your role. The glowing circles represent the number of uses an Ability has. If there is an infinity sign (∞) that means the Ability has unlimited uses.
Night Abilities During the Night phase, you can choose to use your night ability on a player.

Last Will, Notes, and More Your Last Will is a document used to record your actions, observations, and information throughout the game. When you die, your Last Will will be displayed for everyone to see. The Notepad are your private notes and are essential for staying organized and recording information on other players, including your best guess at their role. You can also review your settings, and more depending on your role.

Voting During the Voting phase, you can vote on players to put on Trial. It takes a majority of players voting a player to put them on Trial. Once on Trial, the player can defend themselves before the Town delivers a verdict of Innocent or Guilty. There can be up to 3 Trials per day, but only 1 Trial can end in a Guilty vote.

Town of Salem 2 is much deeper than simply knowing what the buttons do. It is a Social Deduction game at its core, where ‘Good’ players race evil to determine who is lying before they are wiped out.
Discussion and logic are always at odds, Good versus evil, Intelligence versus manipulation.

There are a few basic foundations to keep in mind: <indent=1em>1.</indent><Style="BP">Your goal is (usually) to help your faction be the last one standing.</style> <indent=1em>2.</indent><Style="BP">The <Style="TownColor">Town</style> is our clueless,paranoid, uninformed majority. They vote on who dies during the day, and attempt to deduce who is lying based on evidence and the actions of others.</style> <indent=1em>3.</indent><Style="BP">The rest have significant advantages over any single <Style="TownColor">Townie</style>, but none of it matters if they are put on trial and hanged. In the day they pretend to be Good, acting and voting to hide their identity to buy time to eliminate the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> at night, one by one. They do not care about the truth, as they are the liars the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> seeks.</style> <indent=1em>4.</indent><Style="BP">Players do not usually have a way to indisputably prove their Role / Faction while alive. They can only make claims and try to provide evidence to convince the others.</style> <indent=1em>5.</indent><Style="BP">Each player has a Role with an ability that interacts with other players. This interaction leaves behind facts and evidence the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> can use to determine who is lying. </style> The following section is an introduction to the Logic of Town of Salem 2, as see by a <Style="TownColor">Townie</style>.

Let’s talk about a scenario with no abilities, and therefore no interaction outside what people say. We will also assume the <style="CovenColor">Coven</style> can talk at night.
We now have a situation where there is very little evidence, and the only thing left is discussion. No one will admit to being evil, but there is also no foundation to accuse anyone of wrongdoing nor crimes to be guilty of. The <style="CovenColor">Coven</style> could try to coordonate, but again, without something to accuse someone of the most they can do is gang up on the same person. While this is not unlike a real witch trial, it is a game of he-said she-said.
If we expand this experiment to allow the Evil Roles to kill at night, the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> can still only accuse players at random and hope they are lucky enough to hang the Evil Roles. There is still very little evidence outside of claims and process-of-elimination with the Role List. What is left is still largely a game of luck and mob mentality.
Finally, we allow abilities back in. The Evil Roles visit and kill at night. The Investigative Roles search at random and watch for visits. Protective Roles thwart attacks. Some Roles visit and prevent others from using abilities. The <style="CovenColor">Coven</style> visits players to affect the results of the night, manipulating outcomes or muddying the truth. We have a symphony of information again; Information that can be put to good use.

Let’s talk about Evidence: bits of information that help the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> sniff out the liars. Evidence almost always comes as a result of the actions of players as the game progresses. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">A player’s Role, Last will, and Cause of Death are revealed upon their Death. </style> <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Player abilities and the resulting Visits at night create events that very few people see. Who knows this information and who does not can be very telling. </style> <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Each Role in the Role List is only assigned to one person. Therefore, the Role List can be used via process of elimination alongside the revealed Roles of the dead to know what is possible in a game. </style> <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">The claims of other players. Did someone say they were attacked? Controlled? Role Blocked? What do they claim their Role is? </style> <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Last Wills are records of a player’s experiences revealed upon their death. Do they match up with your own? These can be asked for during discussions. Assume the Will of a dead player is a lie if they are not a <Style="TownColor">Townie</style>. </style> The enemies of the <Style="TownColor">Town</style> are not fools. Most evidence is circumstantial, and a player’s behaviour in Discussions is always worth taking into account.

Many Role abilities require targeting a player at Night, and then ‘Visiting’ them to carry out the action. This could be an attack, protecting someone, investigating, Role-blocking, dousing someone in gasoline, and more.
To resolve these conflicts, we consider if someone is lying, and if so, whom. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Is the claimed Role already dead? That would indicate that both could be lying. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Are there any known Roles that came from the <style="RandomColor">Random</style> card, such as a known <Style="TownColor">Town</style> double or a <Style="TownColor">Town</style> Role that is not listed, like a <Style="TownColor">Bodyguard</style> or a <Style="TownColor">Seer</style>? This would guarantee one of the two is lying. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Ask for their Last Wills, and compare it to what you have seen. Contradictions usually indicate a liar. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Role-specific logic. Does the will or other claims contradict the claimed Role’s rules? <Entry key="GUI_TSS_SOCIAL_WHENCLAIM_TITLE"><![CDATA[When should I Claim?

‘Claiming’ generally means standing up and saying ‘I am a [thing]’ publically. A <Style="TownColor">Townie</style> is at risk of being killed, a non-<Style="TownColor">Townie</style> will lie. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP"><Style="TownColor">Town</style> <style="InvestigativeAlignmentColor">Investigative</style> Roles tend to claim early, and then report their findings each day. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Many Roles will sometimes claim when they have information that contradicts something being said. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Some players claim if they believe it is strategically advantageous to do so. The nuance of this varies by personal preference and by Role. <indent=1em>•</indent><Style="BP">Other than that, usually a player only makes a public claim to their Role when someone else asks them to, or if someone claims their Role as their own.

It is common practice to claim your Sub-Alignment instead of your actual Role. (ex: <Style="TownColor">Town</style> <style="ProtectiveAlignmentColor">Protective</style>, not <Style="TownColor">Bodyguard</style>) This is because two Roles, the <style="CovenColor">Ritualist</style> and the <style="DoomsayerColor">Doomsayer</style>, can kill if they know your true Role.
Once the game reaches a point where it is impossible for either to still be alive in the game, claiming Roles directly becomes safer.
<Style="TownColor">Town</style> <style="InvestigativeAlignmentColor">Investigative</Style> Roles are the exception, since they should be publicly reporting their findings each day.

Welcome to Town of Salem 2 • • • Hey Townies! Welcome to Town of Salem 2! For valuable tips on gameplay and roles, don't forget to check out the Game Guide located in the settings menu for both direct information as well as the Tutorial Video. Enjoy the adventure! Join us on Discord to report bugs, leave feedback, or just join in community conversation. Please remember to leave a review! Thank you and Happy Hanging! • • • Patch v1.5.08 Hey Townies! Today's patch introduces a stronger backend system for the game, this brings in improved security and modernized features. At this time, Town of Salem 2 is now using Lootlocker. Please read the FAQ for the update: • What is a video game backend system? - The backend is the framework that allows the game to work, including login, authorization, security, accounts, inventory, transactions, history, and more. • Why is this happening? - We have been striving to improve the overall systems for the Town of Salem games and this is part of that plan. • What will this do? - This update will give us better tools for moderation, player accounts, player history, and helps ensure we can continue to improve your experience. • What will change from my player perspective? - You may notice improved moderation, more streamlined support & other improvements that are brought on through this update. Otherwise, you should have relatively the same in-game experience. We're continuing to explore & implement more ways to reduce lag. • Do I need to do anything? - Nope! This update does not require any action from individual players. • What if I have a problem with my Town of Salem account after this change? - In the event you have an account issue after this change takes effect, please contact us via the official Town of Salem games Discord by opening a ModMail ticket (instructions within the FAQ channel) OR reach out to us through the support email (support@townofsalem.io). • • • Patch v1.5.07 Hey Townies! This patch brings in some moderation improvements, including hardware bans for multi-accounters. General Changes: • Added Hardware Bans • Made several improvements to backend reporting tools • Updated to Unity 2022.3.63f2 Bug Fixes: • Fixed a bug allowing Coven Leader to retrain any player into any role • Fixed a special character allowing users to spam the chat with walls of spaces (Note: This fix went live on January 14, 2026 after a server restart & all users who abused this exploit have been banned) Role Updates: • Admirer has been overhauled - At the start of the game, a random Townie will be marked as your Obsession. You will learn their sub-alignment, but not their identity - You may Admire another player at night to see if they are your Obsession, if they are - your Admire ability will be replaced with a Care ability - When Caring for your Obsession at night, a Barrier will be placed on both you and them. This ability has 2 charges - If your Obsession dies before you find them, they will be rerolled. If they die after they find them you will be left without an Obsession - During the day you may Bestow another player. This will permanently grant them Astral Visits, Roleblock Immunity, and Control Immunity. This ability has 2 charges • Vampire has been overhauled - Vampire is now a Neutral Outlier, and is also Unique - During the night you may choose to Drain another player, dealing a Basic Attack to them - During the night you may choose to Convert another player. If they are a member of the Town faction they will be converted to the Vampire faction, keeping their original role. If they are not, you will instead Drain them. This ability has 3 charges - If you die, another member of the Vampire faction will become the new Vampire - While Solo, you will have Basic Defence and Detection Immunity. You will lose these if you have at least one teammate • Cursed Soul has been overhauled - Cursed Soul will now only swap roles with their target, not factions - Cursed Soul's win condition is now to kill all players with the Cursed Soul role - Cursed Soul now shares a night chat with other members of the Wandering Souls faction • Astral Visits will now bypass Jail • Death Notes are now exclusive to Neutral Killing roles • Coven Killing roles are now mutually exclusive - Coven Leader will only be able to retrain a CPOW into a CK if there isn't already one in the game • Ritualist's Blood Ritual ability has been reduced to 2 charges • Camouflage has been removed • Mayor will no longer gain votes during a TT Hunt • Monarch will no longer grant vote immunity • Potion Master can now target all living players with their Heal Potion • War now bypasses Jail • Poisoner can now Smog other Coven members, and will know if they have blocked at least one player • Socialite has been reworked: - Players who are blocked by Socialite's Party will no longer be added to the Guest List - Socialite will now only learn if they have rejected at least one person, rather than learning who they are - Socialite can no longer Party on the same player two nights in a row • Added "Factional Defense", a player's natural defense is now derived from the faction they are on rather than their base role - The Town and Coven factions have no defense - The Apocalypse and Vampire factions have basic defence if there is only one living member General Changes: • Fully Overhauled the Game Guide - A 6 lesson visual tutorial on the game has been added - The Info guide has been heavily expanded/updated - The Roles guide has received visual upgrades - The Keywords guide now lets you filter by keyword type • Cursed Soul now has a Silhouette • Cursed Soul and Vampire have new faction colours. • Poisoner's Smog UI has been updated to make it more clear that you cannot attack with the Necromonicon while using it • Role Icons have been added to various interfaces such as the in-game rolelist and bucket display lists • The Roledeck Builder UI now shows the total modifiers in a list • Altered vote weights will now show as (+Y) and (-Y) instead of (xY) and (x-Y) • All feedback messages that specified "Your target" will now directly reference your target by name. - "Sydney seems suspicious!" - "You sense that Curtis and Tuba seem to be enemies!" • Added more abbreviations for quickly mentioning roles and buckets • Updated Witch's "You cannot control someone two nights in a row" message to accommodate Control Immune roles • Cinematics can now have special variations depending on a player's map -
